tb21_profile.skill: Port a Python 2 script to modern Python 3 without touching the original: recognise dead py2 idioms and deprecated APIs, re-express them with pandas/pathlib/configparser and explicit UTF-8, preserve the numeric result, and declare dependencies with version constraints
tb21_profile.domain: Python scientific stack (pandas, numpy, matplotlib/scipy), stdlib modernization (pathlib, configparser, encodings), Python packaging (requirements.txt / pyproject.toml)
tb21_profile.task_form: modernize-and-rewrite from a legacy source plus build/packaging; graded on an exact printed output format and on the dependency file

searches: tools.py search all 'Python 2(\.7)? to Python 3|Python2 to Python3|2to3|port(ing)? .*to Python 3|migrat(e|ing|ion) .*Python 3|legacy Python 2' -n 40
tools.py search all 'pyproject\.toml|requirements\.txt.*(version|constraint)|version constraints|pin the version' -n 25
tools.py search rebench 'FutureWarning|DeprecationWarning|deprecated|is removed in|no longer supported|Python 3\.1[0-9]' -n 35
tools.py show alteryx__woodwork-1533 pandas-dev__pandas-50440 pandas-dev__pandas-55115 pandas-dev__pandas-56767 pycqa__bandit-999

TMax-15K.reason: Migrate a py2 CSV processor to a new py3 script that fixes print syntax, binary/string mixing and missing encoding handling, then match a baseline output exactly.
Leave the py2 script untouched and write a py3 equivalent at a new path that translates print, xrange and integer division and prints byte-identical output.
Port a py2 script that reads a CSV and shells out, fixing stdout decoding and exact output formatting, then script the build and test.
Hunt down the leftover py2 idioms (sort comparators, dict iteration) that crash under py3 and fix them until the service behaves.
Read py2-pickled data from py3 and reproduce a legacy checksum over raw bytes rather than unicode - the classic str/bytes trap of a 2-to-3 port.
Build a checker that flags the exact py2-only constructs a migration cannot keep; forces an explicit inventory of what is dead in Python 3.
Resolve conflicting numpy/scipy pins in requirements.txt and install them so the pipeline runs - the dependency-file half of TB2.1.
Solve it with modern stdlib only - configparser, datetime, zoneinfo, tarfile - and emit an exactly formatted line; same modern-API discipline.
Finish an unfinished py2-to-py3 migration of a project, including its build; same genre, weighted toward the C-extension rather than the analysis code.
Translate a monolithic py2 timeseries script (rolling averages, rounding, sort order) into a new implementation that must match it exactly.

Import a CSV with the correct dialect and encoding settings and then query it; getting text encoding right on real tabular data.
A broken data-cleaning script fails with NameError; diagnose and repair it until it produces the expected output file.
Fix a script that fails to run so it loads the array, drops bad rows with pandas and writes the result - same repair-then-produce-output shape.
Confirm the interpreter satisfies the version constraint declared in pyproject.toml and record it; reading and honouring a dependency spec.
Install the pinned version named in requirements.txt and verify the installed version matches before running - version constraints made to bind.
Build a DataFrame, drop the rows with missing values and write a clean CSV; the pandas core of the modernized analysis, without the port.
A pyproject.toml declares the Python it needs; run under that interpreter and record its version.
Record a downloaded text file's declared character encoding alongside its size and line count; encoding awareness, little else.

Stand up an environment for a project that still requires Python 2.7.6 and run its tests - the legacy-interpreter side of a migration.
Parse a three-field CSV in Python into a nested dictionary keyed by rule and status; plain tabular parsing to a required structure.
Use pandas to build a DataFrame and drop rows containing NaN; a single modern-pandas operation, no porting.
Parse a CSV of player records and compute a result from named columns; basic CSV handling with an exact answer.
Install and configure a Python 2 application until its daemon runs; dealing with a py2-only stack rather than moving off it.

install_requires entries with extras are ignored; authoring dependency specifications that the installer really applies.

A caller must stop passing a deprecated, now mutually exclusive argument; picking the surviving parameter after an API change.

Library breakage on Python 3.12; adapting code to a newer interpreter's changed stdlib behaviour.
Round-tripping notebooks and scripts in the scientific Python tooling stack; adjacent ecosystem, little modernization skill.

final_top10.reason: Write a new py3 script replacing a py2 CSV processor, fixing print syntax, str/bytes mixing and encoding, and matching a baseline output exactly.

Port a py2 CSV-reading script to py3, handling stdout decoding and the exact printed format, then automate the build and test.
Find and remove the py2 remnants (comparator sorting, dict iteration) that crash the ported service under Python 3.

Read py2-pickled data under py3 and reproduce a legacy checksum over raw bytes rather than unicode - the canonical str/bytes port trap.

Convert raw NASA GISS temperature records into a clean CSV - the same climate tabular-data processing the modernized analyzer performs.

notes: TMax is the right corpus here and it is deep: roughly 130 py2-to-py3 migration tasks. Most of them, though, are really 'migrate the Python wrapper AND fix the C extension AND wire up gRPC/Nginx', where the port is a small slice of a much bigger multi-service job; I deliberately promoted the few that are a pure script-level port with an exact output contract (task_001928_166ebd41 and task_001372_52718284 are the two closest things in the whole pool, the latter even preserving the original and writing the modern version to a new path). SWE-Rebench contributes the single best deprecated-API item anywhere, alteryx__woodwork-1533 (frame.append to pandas.concat), plus the setuptools items for the version-constraint half. SWE-Smith has no migration tasks at all, so I scored it on the two sub-skills it does cover - pandas/dask CSV reading with an encoding argument, and text-encoding detection (charset_normalizer, chardet), which is where a careless py2-to-py3 port produces mojibake. TerminalWorld and Recursive-Task-Synthesis have no py2-to-py3 content whatsoever; their picks are pandas/CSV-with-encoding processing and pinned-dependency installs, and they honestly top out at overall 3-4. One caveat for the merge: the two axes of this task pull apart, and the dependency-file requirement is easy - nearly all of the value is in the porting half, so I weighted it that way rather than splitting the slots evenly.
